title: Calibrated restoration eyed for Myanmar representation
summary: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations have decided to pursue a calibrated engagement, step-by-step and progress-based approach to restore Myanmar’s political representation.

blocks.text: Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro answers questions from the media during a press briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City on November 16, 2026

MANILA, Philippines — Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations have decided to pursue a calibrated engagement, step-by-step and progress-based approach to restore Myanmar’s political representation.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said the ASEAN leaders adopted on Sunday a decision and review on the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus (5PC).
“The foreign ministers will continue the constructive and principled engagement with Myanmar in accordance with the Five-Point Consensus,” Lazaro said.
The leaders expressed deep concern over the conflicts and humanitarian situation in Myanmar, and took note of the recommendations during the ASEAN foreign ministers’ meetings on July 21 and Nov. 14.

“We underscored the need for ASEAN to calibrate its engagement with Myanmar based on developments on the ground, in a manner that encourages further progress in the implementation of the 5PC,” they said.

The leaders denounced the acts of violence in Myanmar against civilians and public facilities, and urged all parties involved to take concrete action to immediately halt indiscriminate violence, denounce any escalation, exercise utmost restraint, ensure the protection and safety of all civilians and civilian infrastructure.

They urged all parties to create a conducive environment for the delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people in need in Myanmar and a national political dialogue. They also appreciated the efforts to ensure progress on the implementation of the 5PC in its entirety, with the sole objective of restoring peace, stability and democracy through a Myanmar-owned and -led approach.

“We commended the work of the ASEAN chair, through its Special Envoy (Lazaro), in establishing inclusive engagements with all relevant stakeholders in Myanmar by promoting national inclusive dialogue, reaching out to parties concerned, including regional and international organizations, in a sustainable manner, towards reaching a Myanmar-owned and -led resolution to the situation in Myanmar,” the statement read.
